papers.title: Wear Behavior of a Heat-Treatable Al-3.5Cu-1.5Mg-1Si Alloy Manufactured by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: In this study, the wear behavior of a heat-treatable Al-7Si-0.5Mg-0.5Cu alloy fabricated by selective laser melting was investigated systematically. Compared with the commercial homogenized AA2024 alloy, the fine secondary phase of the SLM Al-Cu-Mg-Si alloy leads to a low specific wear rate (1.8 ± 0.11 × 10−4 mm3(Nm)−1) and a low average coefficient of friction (0.40 ± 0.01). After the T6 heat treatment, the SLM Al-Cu-Mg-Si alloy exhibits a lower specific wear rate (1.48 ± 0.02 × 10−4 mm3(Nm)−1), but a similar average coefficient of friction (0.34 ± 0.01) as the heat-treated AA2024 alloy. Altogether, the SLM Al-3.5Cu-1.5Mg-1Si alloy is suitable for the achievement of not only superior mechanical performance, but also improved tribological properties.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the wear behavior of a heat-treatable Al-Cu-Mg-Si alloy produced by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Wear tests and microstructural characterization were conducted on as-built and T6 heat-treated SLM alloys, compared with commercial AA2024.
summary_en.result: The SLM alloy exhibited lower specific wear rate and coefficient of friction than AA2024, further improved by T6 treatment.
summary_en.validation: Experimental wear testing with SEM analysis.

papers.title: Subsurface Defect Evaluation of Selective-Laser-Melted Inconel 738LC Alloy Using Eddy Current Testing for Additive/Subtractive Hybrid Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Abstract New materials and manufacturing technologies require applicable non-destructive techniques for quality assurance so as to achieve better performance. This study comprehensively investigated the effect of influencing factors including excitation frequency, lift-off distance, defect depth and size, residual heat, and surface roughness on the defect EC signals of an Inconel 738LC alloy produced by selective laser melting (SLM). The experimental investigations recorded the impedance amplitude and phase angle of EC signals for each defect to explore the feasibility of detecting subsurface defects by merely analyzing these two key indicators. Overall, this study revealed preliminary qualitative and roughly quantitative relationships between influencing factors and corresponding EC signals, which provided a practical reference on how to quantitively inspect subsurface defects using eddy current testing (ECT) on SLMed parts, and also made solid progress toward on-line ECT in additive/subtractive hybrid manufacturing (ASHM) for fabricating SLMed parts with enhanced quality and better performance.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on eddy current testing of SLM Inconel alloy for industrial quality control, with no relevance to biomedical implants, porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue, or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM镍基合金的涡流检测方法以提升质量
summary_zh.method: 实验分析激励频率、提离距离等因素对涡流信号的影响
summary_zh.result: 建立了缺陷参数与信号幅值相位的定量关系
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验验证了涡流检测的可行性

summary_en.motivation: To explore the feasibility of using eddy current testing for subsurface defect detection in selective laser melted Inconel 738LC alloy for additive/subtractive hybrid manufacturing.
summary_en.method: Experimental investigation of the effects of excitation frequency, lift-off distance, defect depth, size, residual heat, and surface roughness on impedance amplitude and phase angle of eddy current signals.
summary_en.result: Preliminary qualitative and quantitative relationships were established between influencing factors and eddy current signals, providing a reference for quantitative inspection of subsurface defects.
summary_en.validation: Experimental measurements of impedance amplitude and phase angle for each defect scenario validated the approach.

papers.title: A novel chlorhexidine-hexametaphosphate coating for titanium with antibiofilm efficacy and stem cell cytocompatibility.
papers.abstract: Dental implants are an increasingly popular way to replace missing teeth. Whilst implant survival rates are high, a small number fail soon after placement, with various factors, including bacterial contamination, capable of disrupting osseointegration. This work describes the development of chlorhexidine-hexametaphosphate coatings for titanium that hydrolyse to release the antiseptic agent chlorhexidine. The aim was to develop a coating for titanium that released sufficient chlorhexidine to prevent biofilm formation, whilst simultaneously maintaining cytocompatibility with cells involved in osseointegration. The coatings were characterised with respect to physical properties, after which antibiofilm efficacy was investigated using a multispecies biofilm model, and cytocompatibility determined using human mesenchymal stem cells. The coatings exhibited similar physicochemical properties to some implant surfaces in clinical use, and significantly reduced formation of multispecies biofilm biomass up to 72 h. One coating had superior cytocompatibility, with mesenchymal stem cells able to perform normal functions and commence osteoblastic differentiation, although at a slower rate than those grown on uncoated titanium. With further refinement, these coatings may have application in the prevention of bacterial contamination of dental implants at the time of surgery. This could aid a reduction in rates of early implant failure.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该研究涉及钛植入物的抗菌涂层，但未涉及增材制造或多孔结构，与用户研究方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: No additive manufacturing process (LPBF/SLM), no porous structure design, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), no stress shielding or stiffness matching.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发钛植入物抗菌涂层以减少早期失败。
summary_zh.method: 在钛表面制备氯己定-六偏磷酸钠涂层并表征。
summary_zh.result: 涂层显著减少多菌种生物膜，同时保持间充质干细胞功能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外生物膜模型和干细胞共培养验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop an antibacterial coating for titanium dental implants to reduce early failure due to bacterial contamination.
summary_en.method: A chlorhexidine-hexametaphosphate coating was synthesized on titanium and characterized for physical properties, antibiofilm efficacy, and cytocompatibility.
summary_en.result: The coating significantly reduced multispecies biofilm biomass for up to 72 hours while maintaining mesenchymal stem cell functions and osteoblastic differentiation.
summary_en.validation: Validation was performed using an in vitro multispecies biofilm model and human mesenchymal stem cell cytocompatibility assays.
